external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor device installed on customer sites that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside the organisation's physical control. Firmware signature verification is unknown: "I do not know whether the nodes check a signature on the image before installing it."

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.notes: The authentication used by the serial console is unknown: "I don't know what authentication that console has, if any."

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An organisation operator who views telemetry dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An internet-exposed MQTT broker running on GKE that receives sensor readings and forwards accepted readings to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE and expose to the internet
processes.notes: The broker uses a pre-shared key for node authentication. The key is per fleet rather than per device, and has not been rotated since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that consumes readings and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used by the gateway to check node keys and determine customer ownership.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service onto which the gateway forwards accepted readings for consumption by the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing readings, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The text does not state its storage encryption.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: The sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
data_flows.notes: The authentication key is per fleet, not per device, and has not been rotated since deployment.

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up device information in the device registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: The sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new firmware image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read. It is unknown whether nodes check a signature before installing the image.

data_flows.name: service console
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The console's authentication is unknown: "I don't know what authentication that console has, if any."

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

data_flows.name: query telemetry
data_flows.description: The dashboard queries telemetry in BigQuery.

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The lake contains site addresses and occupancy patterns, which the text identifies as customer data.

assumptions.basis: The device gateway is described as an MQTT broker, which presents a broker protocol rather than a web application interface.
